title: Pre-course 6: Applications of Derivatives and Combinatorics

bigPicture: **f′ controls monotonicity**, **f″ controls convexity**; critical points plus derivative tests locate and classify **extrema**.
Curve sketching combines critical points, the second-derivative test and inflection points.
**Combinatorics** answers “how many ways…”: counting principle → **permutations** (order, all objects) → **variations** (order, subset) → **combinations** (no order, subset).
The **binomial theorem** expands (x + y)ⁿ using binomial coefficients.

concepts.name: Monotonicity via the first derivative
concepts.simple: If the slope is positive the function goes up; if negative it goes down.
exam: Let f be differentiable on an interval I:

concepts.name: Convexity via the second derivative; inflection points
concepts.simple: f″ > 0: the curve bends upwards (convex). f″ < 0: it bends downwards (concave). Where it switches is an inflection point.
concepts.exam: f twice differentiable on I: **f″ > 0 ⇒ convex**, **f″ < 0 ⇒ concave**. A point where **f″ changes sign** is an **inflection point**.
concepts.example: f(x) = x³ − 3x: f″ = 6x: concave for x < 0, convex for x > 0; inflection point at x = 0.

concepts.name: Critical points and derivative tests
concepts.simple: Peaks and valleys can only be where the slope is zero (or undefined), or at the edges. Check how the slope changes sign, or look at f″.
exam: **Critical point:** f′(x₀) = 0 or f′(x₀) does not exist. Local extrema can only occur at critical points (interior) or at the **boundaries** of the domain.
**First derivative test:** f′ changes + → − at x₀: **local max**; − → +: **local min**; no sign change: neither.
**Second derivative test:** f′(x₀) = 0 and f″(x₀) > 0: **local min**; f″(x₀) < 0: **local max**; f″(x₀) = 0: **inconclusive**.
concepts.example: f(x) = x³ − 3x: f′ = 0 at ±1; f″(−1) = −6 < 0 ⇒ local max (−1, 2); f″(1) = 6 > 0 ⇒ local min (1, −2); inflection at (0, 0).

concepts.name: Fundamental counting principle
concepts.simple: If you choose step by step, multiply the number of choices at each step.
concepts.exam: A task with k steps and n₁, n₂, …, nₖ ways per step can be carried out in **n₁ · n₂ · … · nₖ** ways.

concepts.name: Permutations (ordering all objects)
concepts.simple: How many ways can you line up n different things? n! (n × (n − 1) × … × 1). If some are identical, divide by their factorials.
exam: **With repetition** (groups of n₁, …, nₖ identical objects, n₁ + ⋯ + nₖ = n): **n!/(n₁! n₂! ⋯ nₖ!)**.

concepts.name: Variations (ordered selections)
concepts.simple: Choose k out of n where the order matters (like medals). With repetition allowed (like PIN codes) it is nᵏ.
exam: **Without repetition:** **V(n, k) = n!/(n − k)! = n(n − 1)⋯(n − k + 1)**.
concepts.example: Gold/silver/bronze among 8 athletes: V(8, 3) = 8·7·6 = 336. 4-digit PINs: 10⁴ = 10 000. 4 distinct letters out of 26: 26·25·24·23 = 358 800.

concepts.name: Combinations and the binomial theorem
concepts.simple: Choose k out of n when the order does not matter (a committee). The same numbers appear when you expand (x + y)ⁿ.
exam: **C(n, k) = n!/(k!(n − k)!)**: ways to choose k out of n **without regard to order** (no repetition).
(x + y)³ = x³ + 3x²y + 3xy² + y³, coefficients C(3,0), C(3,1), C(3,2), C(3,3) = 1, 3, 3, 1.
concepts.example: 3 students out of 10: C(10, 3) = 120. Committee of 4 out of 12: C(12, 4) = 495. (x − 2)⁴ = x⁴ − 8x³ + 24x² − 32x + 16.

connections: **Session 5:** derivatives and second derivatives are the tools; **Session 3:** monotonicity/convexity definitions.
Combinatorics is the building block of **probability and statistics** later in the assessment year.
**Session 2:** Σ-notation appears in the binomial theorem.

questions: Find and classify critical points; determine convex/concave intervals and inflection points.
Decide permutation vs. variation vs. combination and compute.
Arrangements of words with repeated letters.
traps: Extrema can also lie at the **boundary** of the domain.
Order matters → variation; order does not matter → combination.
mistakes: Calling every point with f′ = 0 an extremum (x³ at 0 has no sign change).
Using n! instead of n!/(n − k)! for medals.

memorize: **f′ > 0 increasing; f″ > 0 convex; f″ sign change = inflection.**

questions.model:
(a) f′(x) = 3x² − 12x + 9 = 3(x − 1)(x − 3) ⇒ x = 1, 3. f″(x) = 6x − 12: f″(1) = −6 < 0 ⇒ local max, f(1) = 4; f″(3) = 6 > 0 ⇒ local min, f(3) = 0.
(b) f″ < 0 for x < 2 (concave), f″ > 0 for x > 2 (convex); inflection at x = 2 (f(2) = 2).
